title: Problem Background
content: Erdős Problem 461 asks whether $f(n,t)$, the count of distinct $t$-smooth components in $\{n+1,\ldots,n+t\}$, grows linearly in $t$. From Erdős–Graham (1980), p.92, who proved the weaker bound $f(n,t) \gg t/\log t$.

mathContext.formalizationNote: The file contains both axiomatized results and fully proved theorems — a strong formalization with infrastructure lemmas for list products and prime factorization.

title: Smooth Component Definition
content: The $t$-smooth component $s_t(n)$ is defined as the product of prime factors of $n$ (with multiplicity) that are strictly less than $t$. Formally, `smoothComponent t n = (n.factors.filter (· < t)).prod`. This extracts the largest divisor of $n$ whose prime factorization consists entirely of primes $< t$.

mathContext.leanSignature: noncomputable def smoothComponent (t n : ℕ) : ℕ := (n.factors.filter (· < t)).prod
mathContext.proofTechnique: filtering the prime factor list and taking the product
mathContext.formalizationNote: Uses `Nat.factors` (the list of prime factors with multiplicity) and `List.filter`/`List.prod`. The definition is noncomputable since `Nat.factors` involves factorization. Handles n = 0 correctly: `Nat.factors 0 = []`, so `smoothComponent t 0 = 1`.

title: Infrastructure Lemmas
content: Two key helper lemmas proved by induction on lists. `list_prod_filter_dvd`: the product of a filtered sublist divides the product of the full list, i.e., $(l.\text{filter}\, p).\text{prod} \mid l.\text{prod}$. `prime_dvd_list_prod_mem`: if a prime $p$ divides the product of a list of primes, then $p$ is a member of that list. Both are fully proved (no `sorry`).

mathContext.proofTechnique: structural induction on lists with case analysis on the filter predicate
mathContext.formalizationNote: Marked `private` since they are internal infrastructure. `list_prod_filter_dvd` uses `mul_dvd_mul_left` and `dvd_mul_of_dvd_right`. `prime_dvd_list_prod_mem` uses `Nat.Prime.dvd_mul` for the inductive step.

title: Smooth Component Divides n
content: Theorem `smoothComponent_dvd`: for $n \neq 0$, $s_t(n) \mid n$. Proved by unfolding `smoothComponent`, applying `list_prod_filter_dvd` to `n.factors`, and rewriting with `Nat.prod_factors`.

mathContext.leanSignature: theorem smoothComponent_dvd (t n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) : smoothComponent t n ∣ n
mathContext.proofTechnique: reduce to list product divisibility via Nat.prod_factors

title: Smooth Component is t-Smooth
content: Theorem `smoothComponent_smooth`: every prime factor $p$ of $s_t(n)$ satisfies $p < t$. Uses `prime_dvd_list_prod_mem` to show $p$ must appear in the filtered list, then extracts the filter predicate $p < t$.

mathContext.latex: p \text{ prime},\, p \mid s_t(n) \implies p < t
mathContext.leanSignature: theorem smoothComponent_smooth (t n p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hd : p ∣ smoothComponent t n) : p < t
mathContext.proofTechnique: membership in filtered list via prime_dvd_list_prod_mem, then extract filter condition
relatedTheorems: y-smooth numbers: all prime factors ≤ y

title: Smooth Component is Positive
content: Theorem `smoothComponent_pos`: $s_t(n) > 0$ for all $t, n$. Since every element in the filtered factor list is a prime (hence $\geq 2 > 0$), the product is positive by `List.prod_pos`.

mathContext.leanSignature: theorem smoothComponent_pos (t n : ℕ) : 0 < smoothComponent t n
mathContext.proofTechnique: product of positive elements is positive

title: No Small Primes in Complement
content: Lemma `no_small_prime_in_complement`: if $p$ is prime with $p < t$ and $p$ divides the product of factors $\geq t$, this is a contradiction. The proof shows $p$ would appear in the complement list, but the filter condition requires all elements $\geq t$, contradicting $p < t$.

mathContext.latex: p < t \wedge p \mid \prod_{q \in \text{factors}(n),\, q \geq t} q \implies \bot
mathContext.proofTechnique: membership via prime_dvd_list_prod_mem, then contradiction with filter condition
mathContext.formalizationNote: Key infrastructure for the maximality theorem `smoothComponent_largest`, showing the complement part (all primes ≥ t) is coprime to any t-smooth divisor.

title: Smooth Component is Maximal (sorry)
content: Theorem `smoothComponent_largest`: if $d \mid n$ and all prime factors of $d$ are $< t$, then $d \mid s_t(n)$. This establishes $s_t(n)$ as the largest $t$-smooth divisor of $n$. Contains `sorry` — the proof strategy (noted in docstring) decomposes $n = s_t(n) \cdot c$ where $c$ has all primes $\geq t$, then uses coprimality of $d$ and $c$ to conclude $d \mid s_t(n)$.

mathContext.latex: d \mid n \wedge (\forall p \text{ prime},\, p \mid d \implies p < t) \implies d \mid s_t(n)
mathContext.leanSignature: theorem smoothComponent_largest (t n d : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) : d ∣ n → (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ d → p < t) → d ∣ smoothComponent t n
mathContext.proofTechnique: coprime decomposition: n = smooth_part × rough_part, then d | n and gcd(d, rough_part) = 1 implies d | smooth_part
mathContext.formalizationNote: The only `sorry` in the file. Would require proving the complement factorization and using Nat.Coprime.dvd_of_dvd_mul_right. An excellent Aristotle candidate.

title: Distinct Count Function
content: Defines $f(n,t) = |\{s_t(m) : n < m \leq n+t\}|$ using `Finset.Icc` for the interval $[n+1, n+t]$, `Finset.image` to compute the set of smooth components, and `Finset.card` for the cardinality.

mathContext.leanSignature: noncomputable def smoothDistinctCount (n t : ℕ) : ℕ := ((Finset.Icc (n + 1) (n + t)).image (smoothComponent t)).card
mathContext.proofTechnique: image cardinality of smooth component over a closed interval
mathContext.formalizationNote: Uses `Finset.Icc` rather than `Finset.range` for a natural match with the interval {n+1, ..., n+t}. Noncomputable since `smoothComponent` is noncomputable.

title: Main Conjecture: Linear Growth
content: Erdős Problem 461: there exists $C > 0$ and $t_0$ such that $f(n,t) \geq C \cdot t$ for all $n$ and $t \geq t_0$. This conjectures that the number of distinct smooth components in a short interval grows linearly, the strongest possible bound since $f(n,t) \leq t$ trivially.

mathContext.latex: \exists C > 0,\, \exists t_0,\, \forall t \geq t_0,\, \forall n,\, f(n,t) \geq C \cdot t
mathContext.leanSignature: def ErdosProblem461 : Prop := ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ t₀ : ℕ, ∀ t : ℕ, t₀ ≤ t → ∀ n : ℕ, C * ↑t ≤ ↑(smoothDistinctCount n t)
mathContext.proofTechnique: existence of a universal constant (asymptotic lower bound)
relatedTheorems: smooth number distribution in short intervals
mathContext.designChoices: Quantifies ∀ n uniformly, requiring the bound to hold for ALL starting points, not just typical ones. This makes the conjecture substantially stronger than an average-case statement.

title: Erdős–Graham Lower Bound
content: The known bound $f(n,t) \gg t/\log t$ for all $n$ and large $t$. This falls a logarithmic factor short of the conjectured linear bound. The gap between $t/\log t$ and $t$ is the central open question.

mathContext.latex: \exists C > 0,\, \exists t_0,\, \forall t \geq t_0,\, \forall n,\, f(n,t) \geq C \cdot \frac{t}{\log t}
mathContext.leanSignature: axiom erdos_graham_lower : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ t₀ : ℕ, ∀ t : ℕ, t₀ ≤ t → ∀ n : ℕ, C * ↑t / Real.log ↑t ≤ ↑(smoothDistinctCount n t)
mathContext.proofTechnique: axiomatized (original proof uses sieve methods and multiplicative function estimates)
relatedTheorems: Tenenbaum's Introduction to Analytic and Probabilistic Number Theory
mathContext.formalizationNote: Axiomatized since the proof requires detailed sieve theory not yet in Mathlib. The statement uses `Real.log` for the natural logarithm.

title: Boundary Cases and Basic Properties
content: Five fully proved boundary results. `smoothComponent_one`: $s_t(1) = 1$. `smoothComponent_t_le_one`: $s_t(n) = 1$ when $t \leq 1$ (no primes below 1). `smoothDistinctCount_le`: $f(n,t) \leq t$ (trivial upper bound from interval size). `smoothDistinctCount_zero`: $f(n,0) = 0$. `smoothComponent_zero`: $s_t(0) = 1$. `smoothComponent_prime`: $s_t(p) = p$ if $p < t$, else $1$.

mathContext.latex: s_t(1) = 1,\quad t \leq 1 \implies s_t(n) = 1,\quad f(n,t) \leq t,\quad f(n,0) = 0
mathContext.proofTechnique: direct computation using Nat.factors properties, Finset.card_image_le, and interval cardinality
mathContext.formalizationNote: All five theorems are fully proved with no sorry. `smoothDistinctCount_le` uses the key fact that image cardinality ≤ domain cardinality and `Finset.card_Icc`. `smoothComponent_prime` uses `Nat.factors_prime` to reduce to a singleton list.

title: Trivial Upper Bound f(n,t) ≤ t
content: The count $f(n,t) \leq t$ since the image of a $t$-element set has at most $t$ elements. This is tight in the sense that the conjecture asks whether $f(n,t) \geq Ct$ — i.e., whether the count is $\Theta(t)$. Proved using `Finset.card_image_le` and `Finset.card_Icc`.

mathContext.leanSignature: theorem smoothDistinctCount_le (n t : ℕ) : smoothDistinctCount n t ≤ t
mathContext.proofTechnique: image cardinality ≤ domain cardinality, combined with interval cardinality calculation
mathContext.formalizationNote: Fully proved. Together with the conjecture $f(n,t) \geq Ct$, this would give $f(n,t) = \Theta(t)$.
